detailed_description:
HTML to Text strips HTML markup to plain text in the browser using a small set of regular expressions. Paste HTML into the left textarea, toggle three options (preserve links rewrites as 'text (url)' otherwise links keep only the inner text; preserve line breaks turns
,

, , , , / into newlines or tabs; preserve lists turns
  • into bullet lines and
      /
        into surrounding blank lines), then click Convert. The tool also drops script/style content, decodes common named and numeric HTML entities, collapses runs of spaces, and trims excessive blank lines. A Copy button copies the output and Load Sample inserts an example HTML page. The tool is regex-based, not a full DOM parser, and does not render tables, images, or CSS; there is no file upload or .txt download.
usage_steps: Paste HTML into the left textarea, or click Load Sample for example markup
Toggle Preserve Links to keep link URLs as 'text (url)' instead of just the text
Toggle Preserve Line Breaks to keep paragraph and block element line breaks
Toggle Preserve Lists to turn <li> items into bullet lines
Click Convert to strip the markup and produce plain text
Click Copy in the output panel to copy the text to the clipboard
usage_examples: Convert a blog post's HTML body into a plain-text version for an email newsletter
Strip markup from a saved HTML snippet to paste into a note-taking app
Keep links as 'text (url)' to make a plain-text reference list out of an article
Quickly turn HTML lists into bullet lines for a meeting summary

faqs.question: How does HTML to Text handle links and lists?
faqs.answer: With Preserve Links enabled, anchors are rewritten as 'text (url)'; with Preserve Lists enabled, <li> items become bullet lines. Both toggles can be combined with Preserve Line Breaks.

faqs.question: Does it keep script and style content?
faqs.answer: No. Script and style blocks are dropped automatically, so only the visible text content remains in the output.

faqs.question: Are HTML entities decoded?
faqs.answer: Yes. Common named entities (such as & and  ) and numeric entities are decoded to their characters.

faqs.question: Is my HTML uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. The conversion runs locally in your browser using regular expressions, and your content never leaves the page.
